record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: How should one analyze buckling of periodic structures made of elastic bars when local buckling modes may have a period different from the period of the underlying bar structure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an elastic structure $\mathcal{S}_\varepsilon$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2$ or $3$) consisting of slender elastic bars arranged in a spatially periodic pattern with period cell $\varepsilon Y$, where $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is a fixed reference cell and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small scale parameter. Each bar is modeled by one-dimensional elasticity (Euler–Bernoulli or geometrically exact beam theory) with prescribed bending and axial stiffness, joined at the nodes of the periodic lattice. The structure is subjected to a macroscopic compressive loading parametrized by $\lambda\ge 0$, and one studies the linearized buckling eigenvalue problem
$$ \mathcal{K}(u) - \lambda \mathcal{G}(u) = 0, $$
where $\mathcal{K}$ is the elastic stiffness operator of the bar network and $\mathcal{G}$ is the geometric (prestress) operator induced by the applied load.

Develop a rigorous homogenization theory for the critical buckling load $\lambda_\varepsilon$ and the associated buckling modes $u_\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$, in the regime where the local buckling modes need not be $\varepsilon Y$-periodic but may have a period that is an integer (or non-integer, quasi-periodic) multiple of the underlying lattice period. Specifically:

(a) Define a notion of effective (homogenized) buckling problem that captures, in the limit $\varepsilon\to 0$, buckling modes whose microscopic profile has period $kY$ for arbitrary $k\in\mathbb{N}$, as well as long-wavelength modes described by Floquet–Bloch quasi-momenta $\theta\in Y^*$ (the dual cell).

(b) Prove convergence (in an appropriate sense) of the discrete critical loads $\lambda_\varepsilon$ to a limit $\lambda_*$ obtained as the infimum over $\theta\in Y^*$ (and over admissible macroscopic stress states) of cell-problem eigenvalues $\lambda(\theta)$, and identify the cell problems explicitly.

(c) Characterize geometric and loading configurations for which the infimum is attained at $\theta=0$ (so that the homogenized buckling load coincides with the classical one-cell-periodic prediction), versus configurations where the infimum is attained at $\theta\neq 0$ (so that subperiodic / long-wavelength local modes determine the critical load and the naive one-cell homogenization underestimates instability).
artifact.category_tag: homogenization and buckling of periodic lattices
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress exists: Floquet–Bloch analysis combined with homogenization has been used to detect microstructural buckling modes of periods larger than the unit cell in cellular cylindrical shells, lattice materials, and beam-based cellular structures. However, a complete rigorous homogenization theory for general periodic bar structures that systematically accounts for all possible subperiodic/quasi-periodic local buckling modes (including non-integer multiples and interactions with macroscopic loading) is not fully established, and the problem is generally treated as an active and partly open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Bloch wave buckling analysis of axially loaded periodic cylindrical shells
status_evidence.snippet: Floquet–Bloch theory used to capture buckling modes spanning over multiple periods of the microstructure.
status_evidence.claim: Bloch-wave methods address local buckling modes with periods different from the unit cell.

status_evidence.title: A homogenization model for multiple buckling response of axially compressed cellular cylindrical shells
status_evidence.snippet: Simplified model based on homogenization, a linearized stability criterion and Floquet–Bloch theory predicts microstructural buckling.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works combine homogenization with Floquet–Bloch to predict subperiodic buckling, indicating progress but not full resolution.

status_evidence.title: Buckling optimization of additively manufactured cellular structures using numerical homogenization based on beam models
status_evidence.snippet: Elastic properties and local buckling behavior are upscaled via homogenization based on geometric exact beam theory.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical homogenization frameworks for bar/beam lattice buckling exist but typically assume cell-periodic modes.
